title: NASA Connect - Crash - ALDF Edutour Activity
description:
NASA Connect segment involving students in a web-based activity called Edutour sponsored by Nauticus. The edutour is a digital tour of the NASA Langley Aircraft Landing Dynamics Facility.

NASA Identifier: NasaConnect-Crash-AldfEdutourActivity

transcript.text: Speaking of the web, NASA Connect travels south to Norfolk, Virginia for today's web-based activity.
Hi!
Norbert and I are here at Nodikas in Norfolk, Virginia.
This maritime center is huge and features over 150 interactive exhibits.
Nodikas and NASA are teaming up for this program of NASA Connect to introduce you to this show's online activity, the NASA Edutory.
The first, with a little help from Norbert, let's take a quick tour of Norbert's online laboratory.
And observe the type of lab features that are just a mouse click away to support the NASA Connect programs.
The digital content found in the lab makes a vast collection of information, ideas, resources and experts accessible to you at any time.

Okay, everybody, as you can see, we are here now inside Nodikas where some students from the Chrome Club have gathered to introduce you to the NASA Edutory, a digital tour of the NASA Langley aircraft lane dynamics facility.
Now, this digital tour has been designed to augment the video presentation and to provide you the user the opportunity to use this information in ways like NASA scientists.
So, let's take a sneak peek at the tour.
From the NASA Connect website, go to Norbert's lab, where you'll find a button that gets you to the ALDF Edutory.
There are four main parts that make up this NASA lab, propulsion, test carriage, track and a restment system.
When you start the tour, you'll get information about how the propulsion system works and also the science behind the system.
Once you've understand that, you'll do an activity that helps you visualize the mathematics and science concepts.
You'll place some animations, then answer questions about what you've observed.
There's an activity for each one of the four parts and related questions that will test your knowledge.
But we want you to see the website for yourself, so that's all we'll show you now.
Oh, by the way, there is a review at the end of the tour that will summarize what you've learned during your visit to the lab.
A special thanks to our university student mentors from the AIAHimpton Road Student Branch, the AIAA as a special connect partner offers its students as mentors to registered connect classrooms.
To learn more about the mentoring program, check out our website.
Bringing to you the power of digital learning, I'm Shelly Kianwright for NASA Connect Online.
Bye!
